items.title: 52035_Eddie Durham oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...Stanfield and Hawkins kind of had a big tone like that.

ctx.x: And the way he'd hit the note, you know. Like, a lot of guys pick it like this? He used to hit those notes. Big, like that. That was the style then, and Mose Allen wasn't a great bass player, but he used that style and -- he didn't play many notes, though.
Well, he sort of -- he slapped more.

Yeah, he didn't have much tone, but Stanfield and Hawkins kind of had a big tone like that. But at the present time, Gene Ramey is the guy with that big solid tone. Not naming other musicians, but he's a little bigger than some of the greater guys in those days.
